Answer: B
Reason: The radiographs show a well-circumscribed, slightly lobulated mass in the superior mediastinum that is located retrotracheally on the lateral view; this specific location and smooth morphology are characteristic of an oesophageal lipoma (or other benign oesophageal lesion), whereas lymphoma typically presents with more diffuse adenopathy and neurogenic tumors are usually posterior/paravertebral.
